userStories.title: Skill catalog data and parsers
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the SkillSource/Skill/ProjectSkill Prisma models and migration, the resolver contract types, and the pure parsers `parseGitHubUrl` and `parseSkillFrontmatter`.

**Motivation** — Brainstorm threads need skills pinned to a git commit; koda has no skill concept today, and a source must be normalized and its SKILL.md parsed deterministically so a skill name means the same content until an admin updates it.

**Approach**

New data:
```prisma
model SkillSource {
  id           String    @id @default(cuid())
  gitUrl       String    // normalized https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>
  owner        String    // lowercase
  repo         String    // lowercase
  ref          String    // branch or tag as entered
  path         String    // repo-relative directory holding skill directories; "" = repo root
  resolvedSha  String?
  resolvedAt   DateTime?
  status       String    // OK | RESOLVE_FAILED
  statusReason String?
  createdById  String
  createdAt    DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime  @updatedAt
  skills       Skill[]
  @@unique([owner, repo, ref, path])
}

model Skill {
  id          String         @id @default(cuid())
  sourceId    String
  name        String         @unique
  description String
  dir         String
  source      SkillSource    @relation(fields: [sourceId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  projects    ProjectSkill[]
  @@index([sourceId])
}

model ProjectSkill {
  projectId   String
  skillId     String
  enabledById String?
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
  skill       Skill    @relation(fields: [skillId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  project     Project  @relation(fields: [projectId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  @@id([projectId, skillId])
  @@index([skillId])
}
```
`Project` (apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma ~110-131) gains the back-relation `skills ProjectSkill[]`. Migration directory: `apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261012090000_skill_catalog/migration.sql`. Statuses are string constants in `src/common/enums.ts` (`SkillSourceStatus`: OK | RESOLVE_FAILED; no Prisma enums, rule api-core).

Errors use the existing App exceptions with the key as prefix, so the message key is `<key>.<status>` in `apps/api/src/i18n/{en,zh}/skills.json`: `ValidationAppException(args, 'skills.unsupportedHost')` carries code `-2` -> key `unsupportedHost.-2` (as `fleet.json` `dispatchInput.-2`). Usage example: apps/api/src/webhook/webhook.service.ts:53.

`parseSkillFrontmatter(text): { name, description }` (`apps/api/src/skills/skill-frontmatter.ts`): a leading UTF-8 BOM is stripped and `\r\n` is normalized to `\n` first; the file must then start with a line `---`; the block ends at the next line `---`; within it, `name:` and `description:` are single-line scalars (optional surrounding single or double quotes are stripped; other keys are ignored). `name` must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`; a missing block, a missing or invalid `name`, a missing or empty `description`, or a block scalar (`description: >` / `|`) -> `invalid_skill` with the skill's `dir` as detail. `description` longer than 1024 characters is truncated to 1024. No YAML dependency is added. (Because `parseSkillFrontmatter(text)` takes only the text, it throws `SkillResolveError('invalid_skill')` without detail; the resolver in US-002 re-throws/attaches the skill `dir` as detail.)

`parseGitHubUrl(url): { owner, repo, gitUrl }` (`apps/api/src/skills/github-url.ts`): accepts only `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` with an optional trailing `.git` or `/`; owner and repo match `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,100}$` and are not `.` or `..` (a repo of only `.git` is rejected); returns them lowercased and `gitUrl = https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>`, built by concatenating a `GITHUB_WEB_BASE = 'https://github.com/'` constant with `owner + '/' + repo` — never a template literal containing `github.com/${`, which the existing tripwire `apps/api/src/vcs/provider-construction-sites.spec.ts` forbids in `src/`. Anything else throws `ValidationAppException({}, 'skills.unsupportedHost')`.

**Scope** — In: Prisma models + migration + Project back-relation, `SkillSourceStatus` constants, resolver contract file (`skill-resolver.ts`), `parseSkillFrontmatter`, `parseGitHubUrl`. Out: the GitHub resolver implementation (US-002), module/service/controllers/i18n json files (US-003), `path`/`ref` DTO validation (US-003), anything web. Feature-level: frontmatter keys other than name/description, duplicate keys, trailing `#` comments, SSH URLs and extra-path-segment URLs get no dedicated handling.

**Interface**
```ts
// apps/api/src/skills/skill-resolver.ts
export interface ResolvedSkill { name: string; description: string; dir: string }
export interface SkillResolution { sha: string; skills: ResolvedSkill[] }
export type SkillResolveReason =
  | 'not_public_or_missing' | 'ref_not_found' | 'rate_limited' | 'tree_truncated' | 'no_skills' | 'too_many_skills'
  | 'invalid_skill' | 'duplicate_name' | 'provider_error' | 'provider_unreachable';
export class SkillResolveError extends Error { constructor(readonly reason: SkillResolveReason, readonly detail?: string) { super(reason); } }
export interface SkillResolver { resolve(input: { owner: string; repo: string; ref: string; path: string }): Promise<SkillResolution> }
export const SKILL_RESOLVER = Symbol('SKILL_RESOLVER');

// apps/api/src/skills/skill-frontmatter.ts
export function parseSkillFrontmatter(text: string): { name: string; description: string };

// apps/api/src/skills/github-url.ts
export function parseGitHubUrl(url: string): { owner: string; repo: string; gitUrl: string };
```

parseGitHubUrl('https://gitlab.com/nathapp-io/skills') throws ValidationAppException with prefix skills.unsupportedHost
parseGitHubUrl('https://github.com/nathapp-io/..') throws ValidationAppException with prefix skills.unsupportedHost
parseSkillFrontmatter on text '---' / 'name: spec-review' / 'description: "Review a spec"' / '---' / '# Body' deep-equals { name: 'spec-review', description: 'Review a spec' }

parseSkillFrontmatter with a description value of 1500 characters returns a description equal to the first 1024 characters of the value
parseSkillFrontmatter on text whose first line is not '---' throws SkillResolveError with reason invalid_skill
parseSkillFrontmatter with 'name: Spec_Review' throws SkillResolveError with reason invalid_skill
parseSkillFrontmatter with 'description: >' followed by an indented line throws SkillResolveError with reason invalid_skill
parseSkillFrontmatter with a name line and no description line throws SkillResolveError with reason invalid_skill
parseSkillFrontmatter with 'description:' followed by no value throws SkillResolveError with reason invalid_skill
Inserting a second SkillSource row with the same owner, repo, ref and path as an existing row fails with a unique-constraint violation
Inserting a Skill row whose name equals the name of a Skill under another source fails with a unique-constraint violation

Applying the 20261012090000_skill_catalog migration with applyMigration to a scratch schema from scratchSchemaBefore creates the SkillSource, Skill and ProjectSkill tables, after which inserting two SkillSource rows with the same owner, repo, ref and path fails with a unique-constraint violation

routing.reasoning: Additive schema + migration and two pure parsers; standard patterns, 5-7 files, no auth or access control.

parseGitHubUrl('https://github.com/o/r/') returns gitUrl 'https://github.com/o/r'

userStories.title: GitHub skill resolver
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Implement `GitHubSkillResolver`, which resolves a (owner, repo, ref, path) to a pinned commit SHA and the list of skills under the path via anonymous GitHub REST calls through `FleetHttpClient`.

**Motivation** — A source must resolve to a pinned commit so a skill name means the same content until an admin updates it; no credential path exists for non-fleet repositories (ruling D546).

**Approach**

`GitHubSkillResolver implements SkillResolver` (`apps/api/src/skills/github-skill-resolver.ts`), through `FleetHttpClient` (`apps/api/src/fleet/git-broker/fleet-http-client.ts:13`: `request(method: 'GET' | 'POST', url, headers: Record<string,string>, body?) => Promise<{status:number; body:unknown}>`, bounded by `FLEET_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS`, never follows redirects, parses JSON, throws `RepoCheckException('provider_unreachable')` on network failure or redirect and `RepoCheckException('provider_error')` on a non-JSON body) with headers `{ accept: 'application/vnd.github+json', 'x-github-api-version': '2022-11-28' }` and no `authorization`. The API base URL is `VCS_CFG` / `IVcsConfig.githubApiUrl` (`apps/api/src/config/vcs.config.ts:5,32`). `GitHubAppClient` (`github-app-client.ts`) `getTree` (`:143`, `GET {api}/repos/{o}/{r}/git/trees/{sha}?recursive=1`, drops non blob/tree entries, reports `truncated`) and `getFile` (`:158`, contents API, base64) are the pattern to mirror; their methods require an App token, so the resolver does not call them but issues the same requests anonymously.

1. `GET {api}/repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}` -> `sha` (the ref is URL-encoded per path segment).
2. `GET {api}/repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{sha}?recursive=1`; `truncated: true` -> `tree_truncated`.
3. A skill = a `tree` entry whose parent directory equals `path` (repo root when `path` is `""`) and for which a `blob` entry `<dir>/SKILL.md` exists. Zero skills -> `no_skills`; more than 50 -> `too_many_skills`. Skills are ordered by `dir`.
4. A `SKILL.md` whose tree entry `size` exceeds 262144 -> `invalid_skill` with detail `<dir>`, before any contents call. For each remaining skill, `GET {api}/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{dir}/SKILL.md?ref={sha}` (`dir` URL-encoded per path segment); a response whose `type` is not `file` (for example a symlink) or whose `size` exceeds 262144 -> `invalid_skill` with detail `<dir>`; otherwise its base64 `content`, decoded as UTF-8 and passed to `parseSkillFrontmatter` (a frontmatter failure surfaces as `invalid_skill` with the skill's `dir` as detail).
5. Two skills in one source with the same `name` -> `duplicate_name` (detail: the name).
6. `statusReason` (stored later by the service) is `reason` or `reason:detail`, truncated to 300 characters.

HTTP mapping for every call: 404 -> `not_public_or_missing`; on the commits call only, 422 (GitHub's answer for a ref that resolves to no commit) -> `ref_not_found`; 403 or 429 -> `rate_limited`; any other non-200 or a body of the wrong shape -> `provider_error`; a `RepoCheckException` from `FleetHttpClient` maps to its own reason (`provider_unreachable` or `provider_error`). A renamed repo (GitHub answers 301) is refused by `FleetHttpClient` redirect handling -> `provider_unreachable`.

Anonymous GitHub calls are limited to about 60 per hour per IP; a resolve costs 2 calls plus one per skill.

The story also adds `FleetHttpClient` to `GitBrokerModule.exports` (baseline `exports: [GitHubAppClient, GitLabAccessChecker, GitLabTokenSource, GitTokenBroker]`; target also includes `FleetHttpClient`).

SEAM-1 (US-001 -> US-002): `GitHubSkillResolver` passes each `SKILL.md` through `parseSkillFrontmatter`; the ACs feed real frontmatter text through the stubbed HTTP client.

**Scope** — In: `GitHubSkillResolver`, `GitBrokerModule` export of `FleetHttpClient`, unit spec over a stubbed `FleetHttpClient`. Out: `SkillsModule` wiring/`SKILL_RESOLVER` binding, the service, routes, persistence (US-003/US-004). Feature-level: no GitHub App or personal token to raise the rate limit; no private repositories; no hosts other than github.com.

**Interface**
```ts
export class GitHubSkillResolver implements SkillResolver {
  resolve(input: { owner: string; repo: string; ref: string; path: string }): Promise<SkillResolution>
}
// from US-001: SkillResolver, SkillResolution, ResolvedSkill, SkillResolveError, SkillResolveReason, SKILL_RESOLVER
```
acceptanceCriteria: GitHubSkillResolver.resolve({ owner: 'o', repo: 'r', ref: 'release/v1', path: 'skills' }) sends its first FleetHttpClient.request as GET <githubApiUrl>/repos/o/r/commits/release/v1
Every FleetHttpClient.request the resolver sends carries headers with no authorization key

With the commits call returning { sha: 'abc' } and the tree for abc (requested with recursive=1) holding skills/a (tree), skills/a/SKILL.md (blob), skills/b (tree without SKILL.md) and other/c/SKILL.md (blob), resolve deep-equals { sha: 'abc', skills: [{ name: 'alpha', description: 'First', dir: 'skills/a' }] } when skills/a/SKILL.md carries name: alpha and description: First
For a skill directory 'skills/my skill', the resolver fetches GET <githubApiUrl>/repos/o/r/contents/skills/my%20skill/SKILL.md?ref=abc

For path '' and a tree listing tree entries b, a, x, x/y and blobs b/SKILL.md, a/SKILL.md, x/y/SKILL.md in that order, with each SKILL.md carrying a distinct valid name, resolve returns skills whose dir values are exactly ['a', 'b']
A 404 from the commits call rejects with SkillResolveError whose reason is not_public_or_missing
A 422 from the commits call rejects with SkillResolveError whose reason is ref_not_found
A 403 from the tree call rejects with SkillResolveError whose reason is rate_limited
A tree response with truncated: true rejects with SkillResolveError whose reason is tree_truncated
A tree with no directory under path holding a SKILL.md rejects with SkillResolveError whose reason is no_skills
A tree with 51 skill directories under path rejects with SkillResolveError whose reason is too_many_skills
Two skill directories whose SKILL.md frontmatter carries the same name 'dup' reject with an error deep-equal to new SkillResolveError('duplicate_name', 'dup')
A tree whose skills/a/SKILL.md entry has size 262145 rejects with an error deep-equal to new SkillResolveError('invalid_skill', 'skills/a')
When FleetHttpClient.request throws RepoCheckException('provider_unreachable'), resolve rejects with SkillResolveError whose reason is provider_unreachable
A 500 from the commits call rejects with SkillResolveError whose reason is provider_error

routing.reasoning: One resolver class plus a one-line module export, tested over a stubbed FleetHttpClient with the request/parse pattern already in GitHubAppClient; anonymous calls carry no credentials, so the security override does not apply.

suggestedCriteria: A contents response whose type is 'symlink' rejects with an error deep-equal to new SkillResolveError('invalid_skill', <dir>)
A contents response with size 262145 rejects with an error deep-equal to new SkillResolveError('invalid_skill', <dir>)
A SKILL.md whose frontmatter is invalid rejects with an error deep-equal to new SkillResolveError('invalid_skill', <dir>)
A 429 from any call rejects with SkillResolveError whose reason is rate_limited
A 404 from the tree call rejects with SkillResolveError whose reason is not_public_or_missing
A 422 from the tree call rejects with SkillResolveError whose reason is provider_error
A tree response whose body is not an object with a tree array rejects with SkillResolveError whose reason is provider_error
GitBrokerModule still exports GitHubAppClient, GitLabAccessChecker, GitLabTokenSource and GitTokenBroker after FleetHttpClient is added to its exports
When FleetHttpClient.request throws RepoCheckException('provider_unreachable') because GitHub answered a redirect, resolve rejects with SkillResolveError whose reason is provider_unreachable

userStories.title: Skill source create and list routes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add `SkillsModule` with the repository, service and `AdminSkillsController` exposing global-admin `POST /admin/skills/sources` (create + resolve) and `GET /admin/skills/sources` (list).

**Motivation** — A global admin registers skill sources that koda resolves to a pinned commit (ruling D540, D546); a source is resolved on create only, never in the background.

**Approach**

`SkillsModule` (`apps/api/src/skills/`) follows repository -> service -> public (rule api-data): `PrismaSkillCatalogRepository` (module-private, pattern `apps/api/src/fleet/repos/prisma-fleet-repo.repository.ts` `AbstractPrismaRepository`), `SkillsService` (exported), `AdminSkillsController`, `ProjectSkillsController` (US-005). It imports `GitBrokerModule` (for `FleetHttpClient`) and `ProjectAccessModule` (for `ProjectMembershipGuard` and `ProjectAccessService.assertProjectAdmin`, as `fleet-repos.module.ts` does), binds `SKILL_RESOLVER` to `GitHubSkillResolver`, and keeps the repository behind a module-private `SKILL_CATALOG_REPOSITORY` token returning service-owned domain types from `skill-catalog.domain.ts` (rule api-data). Multi-row writes (create insert, update replacement) run inside `txManager.run()` (rule api-data). `SkillsModule` is added to `AppModule.imports`. Controllers carry `@ApiTags('skills')`, `@ApiBearerAuth()`, and `@ApiOperation({ summary })` plus `@ApiResponse` per status on every route (rule api-controllers; `spec-integrity.integration.spec.ts`). List queries are bounded (rule api-data): sources `take: 200` ordered by `createdAt`. `Skill` has `@@index([sourceId])`.

Controller pattern (`FleetReposController`, `apps/api/src/fleet/repos/fleet-repos.controller.ts:15-50`): `@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')`, `@Principal() principal: KodaPrincipal`, `JsonResponse.Ok(...)`. Agent principals (API keys) are refused on every skill route (403); non-admin users get 403.

Errors use existing App exceptions with the key as prefix (message key `<key>.<status>` in `apps/api/src/i18n/{en,zh}/skills.json`): `ValidationAppException(args, 'skills.unsupportedHost')` -> `unsupportedHost.-2`; `ConflictAppException(args, 'skills.nameConflict' | 'skills.sourceExists')` -> `.409`; `NotFoundAppException(args, 'skills.notFound' | 'skills.sourceNotFound')` -> `.404`.

| Route | Who | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /admin/skills/sources` | global ADMIN | `{ items: SkillSourceDto[] }`, sources ordered by `createdAt` (at most 200), each with its skills ordered by `name` |
| `POST /admin/skills/sources` `{ gitUrl, ref, path }` | global ADMIN | parse URL; 409 `skills.sourceExists` when `(owner, repo, ref, path)` is registered; resolve; on success insert source `OK` + skills; on `SkillResolveError` insert source `RESOLVE_FAILED` with `statusReason = reason[:detail]` and no skills; 201 `SkillSourceDto` |

Name conflicts: when a resolution contains a name owned by a skill of **another** source, create returns 409 `skills.nameConflict` (params: name, other source's `gitUrl`) and writes nothing.

`statusReason` is stored as `reason` or `reason:detail`, truncated to 300 characters.

`path` validation (in the create DTO): `""` or 1-200 characters of `/`-separated segments, each matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$`, none `.` or `..`, no leading or trailing `/`. `ref`: 1-200 characters, no whitespace, no `..`. Invalid DTOs return 400 before `resolve` is called.

`SkillSourceDto`: `{ id, gitUrl, ref, path, resolvedSha, resolvedAt, status, statusReason, createdAt, skills: SkillDto[] }`; `SkillDto`: `{ id, name, description, dir }`. DTO file: `apps/api/src/skills/dto/skill-source.dto.ts` (`SkillSourceDto`, `SkillSourceListDto`, `SkillDto`, `CreateSkillSourceDto`).

Failure handling: non-GitHub/malformed URL -> 400 `skills.unsupportedHost`, nothing written; private/deleted/misspelled repo, unknown ref, rate limit, unreachable, truncated tree, no skills, bad SKILL.md on create -> source stored `RESOLVE_FAILED` with the reason (201); name owned by another source -> 409 `skills.nameConflict`, nothing changed; same source registered twice -> 409 `skills.sourceExists`. A failed create still stores the source (`RESOLVE_FAILED`), so re-posting the same source returns 409 `skills.sourceExists`; the admin fixes the upstream repo and clicks Update instead.

Tests never call GitHub: integration and e2e suites spy on the booted app's resolver (`jest.spyOn(app.get(SKILL_RESOLVER), 'resolve')`, pattern of `fleet-pr-refresher.integration.spec.ts:57`). `endpoint.e2e.spec.ts` gains GET /api/admin/skills/sources (200) and POST /api/admin/skills/sources (201 with the resolver spied, and 400 for a GitLab URL). After the API contract change run `bun run api:export-spec` to regenerate `openapi.json`. The unit DI spec uses `GlobalStubsModule` (`apps/api/src/common/test-helpers/global-stubs.module.ts`).

SEAM-2 (US-001, US-002 -> US-003): `SkillsService` parses the request with `parseGitHubUrl` and resolves through the `SKILL_RESOLVER` token bound to `GitHubSkillResolver`.

**Scope** — In: module, repository, domain types, service create/list, `AdminSkillsController` create/list routes, DTOs, en/zh `skills.json`, `AppModule` import, e2e + openapi updates. Out: update/delete routes and replacement transaction (US-004), project skill routes (US-005), web (US-006/US-007). Feature-level: >200 sources not listed; concurrent duplicate creates may 500; no private repos; no background re-resolution.

**Interface**
```ts
// SkillsModule providers
{ provide: SKILL_RESOLVER, useClass: GitHubSkillResolver }
// module-private token in skill-catalog.domain.ts
export const SKILL_CATALOG_REPOSITORY = Symbol('SKILL_CATALOG_REPOSITORY');
// SkillsService (exported); illustrative method names, not mandated by the spec
class SkillsService {
  createSource(input: { gitUrl: string; ref: string; path: string }, principal: KodaPrincipal): Promise<SkillSourceDomain>
  listSources(): Promise<SkillSourceDomain[]>
}
```
acceptanceCriteria: Test.createTestingModule({ imports: [GlobalStubsModule, SkillsModule] }) compiles and get(SKILL_RESOLVER) returns an instance of GitHubSkillResolver

POST /api/admin/skills/sources with the spied resolve rejecting new SkillResolveError('invalid_skill', 'skills/x') returns 201 with statusReason 'invalid_skill:skills/x'

The existing endpoint lifecycle expectations in endpoint.e2e.spec.ts are unchanged after the skills endpoints are added

modifiedFiles.reason: the endpoint lifecycle suite must cover every endpoint (rule api-testing); this story adds GET /api/admin/skills/sources (200) and POST /api/admin/skills/sources (201 with the booted app's SKILL_RESOLVER resolve spied through jest.spyOn(app.get(SKILL_RESOLVER), 'resolve'), and 400 for a GitLab URL), so the suite never calls GitHub. Existing expectations unchanged.

userStories.title: Skill source update and delete routes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add global-admin `POST /admin/skills/sources/:id/update` (re-resolve and replace skills) and `DELETE /admin/skills/sources/:id` (cascade delete).

**Motivation** — A source is re-resolved only when the admin clicks Update, so a skill name means the same content until an admin updates it; project enablements must survive an update for names that persist.

**Approach**

| Route | Who | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /admin/skills/sources/:id/update` | global ADMIN | re-resolve; success -> replace the source's skills (below), `status OK`, new `resolvedSha`/`resolvedAt`; failure -> `status RESOLVE_FAILED` + reason, existing pin and skills kept; 200 `SkillSourceDto`; 404 unknown id |
| `DELETE /admin/skills/sources/:id` | global ADMIN | delete source (skills and project enablements cascade); 204; 404 unknown id |

Name conflicts: when a resolution contains a name owned by a skill of **another** source, update returns 409 `skills.nameConflict` (params: name, other source's `gitUrl`) and changes nothing (status and pin untouched).

Update replacement, in one transaction (`txManager.run()`, rule api-data): skills whose name survives are updated in place (same `Skill.id`, new `description` and `dir`), so their `ProjectSkill` rows survive; new names are inserted; vanished names are deleted (their `ProjectSkill` rows cascade). The repository (`prisma-skill-catalog.repository.ts`) gains the replacement transaction; `skills.service.ts` gains update and delete; `admin-skills.controller.ts` gains the two routes (with `@ApiOperation` and `@ApiResponse` per status, `@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')`). Agent principals are refused (403); non-admin users get 403.

`statusReason` is stored as `reason` or `reason:detail`, truncated to 300 characters. On resolve failure the status is set to `RESOLVE_FAILED` with the reason but the existing `resolvedSha`, `resolvedAt` and skills are kept. Failure handling on Update: private/deleted/misspelled repo, unknown ref (422), rate limit (403/429), unreachable/timeout, truncated tree, no skills, bad SKILL.md -> `RESOLVE_FAILED` with the reason, pin kept (HTTP 200). Renamed repo (301) -> `provider_unreachable`; the admin registers the new URL.

Tests never call GitHub: spy on the resolver (`jest.spyOn(app.get(SKILL_RESOLVER), 'resolve')`). `endpoint.e2e.spec.ts` gains POST /api/admin/skills/sources/:id/update (200 with the resolver spied as in US-003, 404 for an unknown id) and DELETE /api/admin/skills/sources/:id (204, 404 for an unknown id). Regenerate `openapi.json` via `bun run api:export-spec`.

**Scope** — In: update + delete service methods, repository replacement transaction, two controller routes, e2e and openapi updates. userStories.title: Project skill enablement routes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add `ProjectSkillsController` with project-scoped routes to list catalog skills with their enabled flag and to enable/disable a skill for a project.

**Motivation** — Projects enable individual catalog skills (ruling D540); brainstorm threads later read a project's enabled skills as a pinned snapshot.

**Approach**

| Route | Who | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /projects/:slug/skills` | project member, global ADMIN | `{ items: ProjectSkillDto[] }`, every catalog skill ordered by `name`: `{ id, name, description, enabled, source: { id, gitUrl, ref, resolvedSha, status } }` |
| `PUT /projects/:slug/skills/:skillId` | project ADMIN, global ADMIN | upsert the `ProjectSkill` row (`enabledById` = caller); 200 `ProjectSkillDto`; idempotent; 404 `skills.notFound` for an unknown skill |
| `DELETE /projects/:slug/skills/:skillId` | project ADMIN, global ADMIN | delete the row if present; 204; idempotent; 404 `skills.notFound` for an unknown skill |

Membership and admin checks follow the `addProjectAgent` pattern (`apps/api/src/projects/projects.controller.ts:185-204`): `@UseGuards(ProjectMembershipGuard)`, `@CurrentProject() ctx`, then `projectsService.assertProjectAdmin(ctx.project.id, principal)` (`apps/api/src/projects/project-access.service.ts`, `ProjectAccessService.assertProjectAdmin`; guard in `project-membership.guard.ts`). Each handler also refuses a non-user principal with `ForbiddenAppException` (403) when `isUserPrincipal` is false (`apps/api/src/auth/principal/koda-principal.types.ts`): with `AGENT_PROJECT_SCOPING=off` the membership guard admits agents, and the `assertUser` helpers in the fleet controllers (`apps/api/src/fleet/logs/fleet-job-logs.controller.ts:17`) are module-private. Enablement is per project: enabling in project A does not affect project B, and project A's ADMIN cannot manage project B's skills.

The project-skills list query is bounded (`take: 10000` = 200 sources x 50 skills; `ProjectSkill` has `@@index([skillId])`). Controller carries `@ApiTags('skills')`, `@ApiBearerAuth()`, `@ApiOperation` and `@ApiResponse` per status. DTO file `apps/api/src/skills/dto/project-skill.dto.ts` (`ProjectSkillDto`, `ProjectSkillListDto`). `skills.service.ts` gains the project methods; the repository gains the matching queries (module-private, domain types). Wire `ProjectSkillsController` into `SkillsModule`. `endpoint.e2e.spec.ts` gains the three project skill routes (happy path plus one error each); regenerate `openapi.json` via `bun run api:export-spec`; run `bun run generate` as needed (CLI gains no commands; do not edit `apps/cli/src/generated/`).

SEAM-4 (US-005 -> US-007): the project routes are consumed by `useProjectSkills`.

**Scope** — In: three project routes, DTOs, service/repository methods, controller wiring, e2e + openapi updates. Out: catalog source routes (US-003/US-004), web panel and composable (US-007). Feature-level: deleting a non-enabled skill returns 204 (idempotent) with no dedicated AC; per-thread skill selection is out; the runner-side fetch and thread snapshot belong to `fleet-s5a-native-chat`.

**Interface**
```ts
// illustrative method names, not mandated by the spec
class SkillsService {
  listProjectSkills(projectId: string): Promise<ProjectSkillDomain[]>
  enableProjectSkill(projectId: string, skillId: string, userId: string): Promise<ProjectSkillDomain>  // 404 skills.notFound
  disableProjectSkill(projectId: string, skillId: string): Promise<void>                                // 404 skills.notFound
}
// ProjectSkillDto: { id, name, description, enabled, source: { id, gitUrl, ref, resolvedSha, status } }
```
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/projects/:slug/skills by a DEVELOPER member, with catalog skills beta (enabled for the project) and alpha (not enabled), returns items whose [name, enabled] pairs are exactly [['alpha', false], ['beta', true]]
Each item of GET /api/projects/:slug/skills carries source deep-equal to { id, gitUrl, ref, resolvedSha, status } of the skill's source
GET /api/projects/:slug/skills by an authenticated user who is not a member of the project and not a global ADMIN returns 403
GET /api/projects/:slug/skills with an agent API key returns 403 even when the agent is on the project's roster
PUT /api/projects/:slug/skills/:skillId by a project ADMIN returns 200 with enabled: true
After PUT /api/projects/:slug/skills/:skillId by a project ADMIN, the stored ProjectSkill row's enabledById is the caller's user id
Calling PUT /api/projects/:slug/skills/:skillId twice for the same skill leaves exactly one ProjectSkill row
PUT /api/projects/:slug/skills/:skillId by a global ADMIN who is not a member of the project returns 200
PUT /api/projects/:slug/skills/:skillId by a DEVELOPER member returns 403
PUT /api/projects/:slug/skills/:skillId with an agent API key returns 403
PUT /api/projects/:slug/skills/:skillId with a skillId that does not exist returns 404
DELETE /api/projects/:slug/skills/:skillId by a project ADMIN returns 204 and the ProjectSkill row no longer exists
DELETE /api/projects/:slug/skills/:skillId with a skillId that does not exist returns 404
After PUT /api/projects/a/skills/:skillId by project A's ADMIN, GET /api/projects/b/skills returns that skill with enabled: false
PUT /api/projects/b/skills/:skillId by a user who is ADMIN of project A and DEVELOPER of project B returns 403

DELETE /api/projects/:slug/skills/:skillId with an agent API key returns 403
DELETE /api/projects/:slug/skills/:skillId for a skill that is not enabled returns 204

userStories.title: Web project Skills tab and admin navigation
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the project settings Skills tab (`ProjectSkillsPanel` with a new Switch component and `useProjectSkills`) and the admin-only Skills navigation link and command-palette entry.

**Motivation** — Project admins enable individual catalog skills per project, and global admins need navigation to the catalog page.

**Approach**

- `composables/useProjectSkills.ts`: `list(slug)`, `enable(slug, skillId)` (`PUT /projects/<slug>/skills/<skillId>`), `disable(slug, skillId)` (`DELETE /projects/<slug>/skills/<skillId>`), via `useApi()`; `list` is `GET /projects/<slug>/skills` returning `items`.
- `components/ui/switch/` (new, `Switch.vue` + `index.ts`): the shadcn-vue Switch, hand-written over radix-vue's `SwitchRoot` / `SwitchThumb` following the existing `components/ui/*` layout (no shadcn CLI, no network).
- `components/ProjectSkillsPanel.vue` in the new settings tab (trigger label key `skills.project.tab`): one row per catalog skill (name, description, source URL + short SHA (first 7 characters) or `—` when `resolvedSha` is null, status warning (`skills.project.sourceFailed`) when the source is `RESOLVE_FAILED`) with a switch; switches are disabled unless `useProjectViewerRole(slug)` (`apps/web/composables/useProjectViewerRole.ts`) reports `canManage` (project ADMIN or global ADMIN); toggling calls enable/disable and shows a toast (with `extractApiError`) on failure, reverting the switch.
- `pages/[project]/settings.vue` (Tabs at ~:76-110, currently `project`, `vcs`): a third tab `skills` rendering `ProjectSkillsPanel` receiving the project slug; the `TabsList` class changes from `grid-cols-2` to `grid-cols-3`.
- `layouts/default.vue` (ADMIN section links, ~:175-186, `v-if="isGlobalAdmin"`): an ADMIN link `/admin/skills` (label `nav.skills`) after the fleet admin links, shown only to global admins. `components/CommandPalette.vue` (~:27 global entries): a palette entry with id `skills` to `/admin/skills` listed only for global admins (`CommandPalette` reads `useAuth().user.value?.role === 'ADMIN'`, as `layouts/default.vue:51` does). Test pattern: `tests/layouts/default-fleet-nav.spec.ts`.
- i18n keys in `i18n/locales/en.json` and `zh.json`: `nav.skills` and the `skills.project.*` keys including `skills.project.tab` and `skills.project.sourceFailed`; both locale files change together (locale-parity tests). US-006's `skills` admin keys already exist.

SEAM-4 (US-005 -> US-007): the project routes are consumed by `useProjectSkills`; ACs assert `PUT` and `DELETE` on `/projects/<slug>/skills/<skillId>`.

Failure handling (web): toggle fails -> toast with `extractApiError`, switch reverts. The UI is a convenience; the API enforces all permissions.

**Scope** — In: `useProjectSkills`, Switch UI component, `ProjectSkillsPanel`, settings tab wiring, nav link, command-palette entry, en/zh keys, specs. Out: the admin catalog page, `useSkillCatalog` and `AddSkillSourceDialog` (US-006); all API work. Feature-level: no per-thread skill selection; no CLI commands.

**Interface**
```ts
// composables/useProjectSkills.ts
export function useProjectSkills(): {
  list(slug: string): Promise<ProjectSkillDto[]>
  enable(slug: string, skillId: string): Promise<ProjectSkillDto>
  disable(slug: string, skillId: string): Promise<void>
}
// ProjectSkillDto: { id, name, description, enabled, source: { id, gitUrl, ref, resolvedSha, status } }
// components/ui/switch/index.ts exports Switch (radix-vue SwitchRoot + SwitchThumb)
```
acceptanceCriteria: pages/[project]/settings.vue renders three tab triggers, 'project', 'vcs' and 'skills', and the skills content is ProjectSkillsPanel receiving the project slug

The default layout rendered for a user who is not a global admin contains no link to /admin/skills
CommandPalette opened by a global admin lists an entry with id 'skills' that navigates to /admin/skills

analysis:
Greenfield feature inside an existing NestJS 11 + Fastify + Prisma API (apps/api) and Nuxt 3 web app (apps/web). No skill concept exists today: no model, route or page. Everything runs in the API/web; nothing runs on a fleet runner.

Key existing code (verified by spec on main 3162822d):
- apps/api/src/fleet/git-broker/fleet-http-client.ts:13 FleetHttpClient.request(method, url, headers, body?) -> {status, body}; bounded by FLEET_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS, never follows redirects, parses JSON, throws RepoCheckException('provider_unreachable') on network failure/redirect and RepoCheckException('provider_error') on non-JSON body.
- apps/api/src/fleet/git-broker/github-app-client.ts: getTree (:143) and getFile (:158) are the request/parse pattern to mirror, but they require an App token so the resolver issues the same requests anonymously via FleetHttpClient.
- apps/api/src/fleet/git-broker/git-broker.module.ts: exports must gain FleetHttpClient (US-002).
- apps/api/src/config/vcs.config.ts:5,32 VCS_CFG / IVcsConfig.githubApiUrl.
- apps/api/src/fleet/repos/fleet-repos.controller.ts:15-50 global-admin CRUD pattern (@RequiredPermission('ADMIN'), @Principal(), JsonResponse.Ok); fleet-repos.module.ts shows ProjectAccessModule import.
- apps/api/src/projects/projects.controller.ts:185-204 addProjectAgent: @UseGuards(ProjectMembershipGuard), @CurrentProject() ctx, projectsService.assertProjectAdmin(ctx.project.id, principal) (ProjectAccessService.assertProjectAdmin).
- apps/api/src/auth/principal/koda-principal.types.ts isUserPrincipal: each project-skill handler must refuse non-user principals with ForbiddenAppException (AGENT_PROJECT_SCOPING=off admits agents through the guard; assertUser helpers in fleet controllers are module-private).
- apps/api/src/vcs/provider-construction-sites.spec.ts is a tripwire forbidding the literal 'github.com/${' in src/: build gitUrl by concatenating a GITHUB_WEB_BASE='https://github.com/' constant with owner + '/' + repo.
- Errors: ValidationAppException(args, 'skills.unsupportedHost') -> key unsupportedHost.-2; ConflictAppException -> .409 (skills.nameConflict, skills.sourceExists); NotFoundAppException -> .404 (skills.notFound, skills.sourceNotFound). Messages in apps/api/src/i18n/{en,zh}/skills.json (pattern: invites.json, fleet.json).
- Statuses are string constants in apps/api/src/common/enums.ts (no Prisma enums).
- Module layering rule api-data: repository (module-private, token SKILL_CATALOG_REPOSITORY, returns service-owned domain types from skill-catalog.domain.ts) -> service (exported) -> public controllers. Multi-row writes inside txManager.run(). List queries bounded (sources take 200 ordered by createdAt; project skills take 10000).
- Controllers need @ApiTags('skills'), @ApiBearerAuth(), @ApiOperation and @ApiResponse per status (spec-integrity.integration.spec.ts).
- apps/api/test/e2e/api-endpoint/endpoint.e2e.spec.ts must cover every new endpoint (rule api-testing); resolver is spied via jest.spyOn(app.get(SKILL_RESOLVER), 'resolve') (pattern: test/integration/fleet/fleet-pr-refresher.integration.spec.ts:57). Tests never call GitHub.
- openapi.json is committed; regenerate with `bun run api:export-spec` (or `bun run generate`) after API contract changes in US-003/004/005. Never hand-edit apps/cli/src/generated/. CLI gains no commands.
- Prisma: new migration 20261012090000_skill_catalog; Project gains back-relation skills ProjectSkill[]. Integration suites build schema from schema.prisma; migration test uses scratchSchemaBefore/applyMigration from apps/api/test/helpers/migration-schema.ts and createTestPrismaClient from test-prisma.ts.
- Web: pages/admin/fleet/repos.vue + composables/useFleetRepos.ts (admin table pattern incl. 403 -> adminOnly note); pages/[project]/settings.vue:76-110 Tabs (project, vcs) gains skills tab, TabsList grid-cols-2 -> grid-cols-3; layouts/default.vue:175-186 ADMIN links (v-if=isGlobalAdmin; admin check at :51); components/CommandPalette.vue:27 global entries (admin check useAuth().user.value?.role === 'ADMIN'); components/ProjectMembersPanel.vue confirm-dialog/toast patterns; composables/useProjectViewerRole.ts canManage; tests/layouts/default-fleet-nav.spec.ts layout test pattern. components/ui/switch/ is new, hand-written over radix-vue SwitchRoot/SwitchThumb (no shadcn CLI, no network). i18n en.json and zh.json must change together (locale-parity tests); apps/web has its own i18n separate from API.

Risks: (1) US-005 shares skills.service.ts, endpoint.e2e.spec.ts and openapi.json with US-003/004, hence serialization via dependencies. (2) US-006 and US-007 both edit the web locale files; US-007 depends on US-006. (3) Update replacement must keep Skill.id for surviving names so ProjectSkill rows survive; vanished names cascade. (4) Name conflicts across sources must write nothing (create) and change nothing (update). (5) Anonymous GitHub rate limit ~60/h per IP; resolve costs 2 calls + 1 per skill. (6) Concurrent duplicate creates may 500 (accepted, out of scope). (7) Security: all routes are access-controlled (global ADMIN / project ADMIN / member, agents refused) so API stories use three-session-tdd.

Migration path: purely additive (new tables), no backfill. Rollback = drop the three tables.
outOfScope: US-003 only: two concurrent creates of the same source, or two concurrent writes that both introduce the same skill name, may return 500 to the losing request instead of 409; the `(owner, repo, ref, path)` and `Skill.name` unique indexes still guarantee consistent rows.
US-001 only: a `git@github.com:` SSH URL and a URL with extra path segments are rejected by the same validation as any non-matching URL; only the GitLab case is pinned by an acceptance criterion.
US-001 only: frontmatter keys other than `name` and `description`, duplicate keys and trailing `#` comments are not interpreted (the first `name:` / `description:` line wins).
US-004 only: rollback of a partially applied Update after a database failure is not covered by an acceptance criterion; the replacement runs in one transaction.
US-005 only: deleting a skill that is not enabled returns 204 (idempotent) without a dedicated acceptance criterion.
US-003 only: more than 200 registered sources — the admin list shows the first 200 by creation time.
Private skill sources and any credential use for skill repositories (ruling D546); a later feature adds them.
Skill hosts other than github.com (GitLab, generic git URLs).
Editing, uploading or authoring skill content in koda.
Background or scheduled re-resolution of sources; a source changes only on an admin's Update.
The runner-side skill fetch, the thread skill snapshot, and the `load_skill` / `read_skill_file` agent tools — they belong to feature `fleet-s5a-native-chat`.
Using a GitHub App or personal token to raise the anonymous GitHub rate limit.
